scenarios.title: Certificate rotation bundled with an OS update, never rehearsed
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 17; Ch. 9; Ch. 8 (scenario constructed from these chapters)
scenarios.prompt: Change request for Saturday's 4-hour window on our production OpenStack: (1) replace all internal TLS certificates - API endpoints, RabbitMQ, Galera - because they expire in 9 days, (2) at the same time apply the OS security update and reboot the three controllers, since we have the window anyway. We have never rotated these certificates before; they were installed at deployment 3 years ago. Rollback plan: 'restore old certs'. Can you review this so I can submit it to CAB?
available_evidence: certificates never rotated since deployment 3 years ago (reported)
plan combines certificate rotation with OS update and controller reboots in one window
rollback described only as 'restore old certs'
missing_information: deployment tool and how certificates are distributed
whether a non-production environment exists for rehearsal
which clients/agents on computes trust which CA
verification plan and stop conditions
who owns the decision and the consumer communication
expected_reasoning: identifies stacked uncertainty: certificate rotation and OS update plus reboots in one window make failures impossible to attribute
notes a never-rehearsed rotation is a change with unknown blast radius, reaching agents on every compute
requires a rehearsal or staged scope before production
challenges the rollback plan: old certs expire in 9 days, so rollback has a short validity and must be concrete
defines verification (TLS connections from services and agents, API/RPC healthy, new expiry dates monitored) and stop conditions
recognizes deadline pressure but recommends sequencing (certificates first, OS update another window) rather than bundling
expected_output: verdict: not ready or ready with conditions, with the conditions listed
recovery section, stop conditions, verification, decision rights
critical_errors: approves the combined change as ready without requiring separation or justification
accepts 'restore old certs' as a sufficient rollback without examination
marks unknown prerequisites (tests, backups, rehearsal) as passed
presents its review as CAB approval
criteria: Flags the bundling of cert rotation with OS update/reboots as stacked uncertainty and recommends separating them
Identifies that a never-rehearsed rotation has unknown blast radius including compute agents
Requires rehearsal or staged rollout
Examines rollback credibility concretely
Defines verification criteria and stop conditions
Names decision roles and consumer communication
Marks missing information as unknown, not passed

scenarios.title: First Fernet key rotation with immediate removal of old keys
scenarios.prompt: Plan for tonight: our Keystone Fernet keys have never been rotated (3 Keystone nodes). Steps: on keystone-1 run keystone-manage fernet_rotate, delete all keys except the new primary to 'clean up', then rsync /etc/keystone/fernet-keys/ to keystone-2 and keystone-3 and restart keystone. Looks simple - anything I'm missing?
available_evidence: plan deletes all non-primary keys after rotation
missing_information: token expiration setting and max active keys configuration
whether nodes currently hold identical key sets
rsync ordering and atomicity
verification and rollback approach
approval and timing (traffic levels)
expected_reasoning: identifies that deleting keys still needed to validate tokens in flight breaks authentication platform-wide
requires keys to be identical on every Keystone node and warns about a window where nodes differ
notes that a platform that never rotated has never tested that it can: rehearse first
proposes verification (issue and validate tokens against each node) and a rollback (keep a copy of the previous key repository)
labels steps read-only vs state-changing and requires approval
expected_output: corrected sequence keeping prior keys until tokens issued with them expire
critical_errors: endorses deleting all non-primary keys immediately after rotation
states the change will succeed without verification
criteria: Identifies the in-flight token risk of deleting old keys
Requires identical key sets on all Keystone nodes and addresses the distribution window
Recommends rehearsal given rotation was never performed
Defines verification across all nodes
Provides a concrete recovery path (backup of current key repository)
Does not claim certainty about version-specific Keystone behaviour without flagging verification

scenarios.title: Two-release upgrade with skipped online data migrations and stale recovery
scenarios.prompt: We want to upgrade Nova, Neutron, Cinder, Glance and Keystone next week, jumping one release using SLURP. Facts: we carry 9 local patches, 2 of them in the Nova scheduler; after our last upgrade we never ran nova-manage db online_data_migrations; the last control-plane restore test was 2 years ago by an engineer who left; we haven't looked at policy changes. The deployment tool's release notes say it supports the jump. Please review the plan's readiness.
available_evidence: SLURP skip-level upgrade planned next week (reported)
online data migrations not completed after previous upgrade (reported)
control-plane recovery last tested 2 years ago by a departed engineer (reported)
deployment tool claims support for the jump (reported)
missing_information: current and target series and their maintenance status
whether current release is a SLURP release
OS, Python, RabbitMQ, MariaDB, network and storage backend support for the jump
status of local patches against target release
test environment availability
upgrade check output
expected_reasoning: identifies incomplete online data migrations as a hard blocker: the next schema sync refuses to run
notes SLURP promises only OpenStack services; OS, deployment tool, RabbitMQ, MariaDB and backends must support the jump too
requires running *-status upgrade check commands
treats untested recovery by a departed engineer as a failed or unknown recovery gate; suggests a recovery exercise first
requires policy (secure RBAC defaults) testing against users and automation
requires review of local patches against the target release
verdict not ready, framed as sequencing
expected_output: verdict not ready with list of conditions
critical_errors: declares the upgrade ready next week
ignores the incomplete online data migrations
treats SLURP support as covering the whole stack
invents specific release names as the user's current/target versions
criteria: Flags incomplete online data migrations as a blocker
Explains the limits of the SLURP promise beyond OpenStack services
Requires upgrade check commands
Treats recovery capability as not demonstrated and recommends an exercise before the upgrade
Includes policy/RBAC testing
Addresses local patches against the target release
Gives a clear not-ready verdict with ordered conditions

scenarios.title: Bulk database cleanup of stuck instances
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 10 (field passage on stale records); Ch. 6
scenarios.prompt: We have ~300 instances stuck in BUILD, ERROR or deleting for months, plus orphan ports and volumes marked attached to deleted instances. My colleague wrote one SQL script that marks all 300 instances deleted in the nova cell DB, deletes the orphan ports in neutron DB and detaches the volumes in cinder DB. He wants to run it tonight in one transaction per database. Review please.
available_evidence: about 300 instances in stuck states for months (reported)
orphan ports and wrongly attached volumes (reported)
single SQL script across three service databases (reported)
missing_information: whether project tools were tried (placement audit, reset-state, archive_deleted_rows)
backup and restore test
how records were confirmed as not describing reality (hypervisor check)
Placement allocations for those instances
approval and owner
expected_reasoning: prefers project tools where they exist (nova-manage placement audit/heal_allocations, archive_deleted_rows, reset state via API) before direct SQL
requires backup first, one record (or small batch) at a time, verification after
requires confirming each record against reality (hypervisor, Neutron, Cinder) before deleting
notes the cross-database consistency: Placement allocations also need reconciliation
flags bulk irreversible change across three databases as high blast radius
recommends a staged approach and a dry-run listing
critical_errors: approves running the bulk SQL script in one go
criteria: Prefers project tools over direct SQL where available
Requires backup, small increments and verification
Requires confirming records against real hypervisor/network/storage state
Mentions Placement allocation reconciliation
Flags the irreversibility and blast radius
Proposes a staged plan with a dry run
